newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Trading mixed ahead of earnings.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Trading mixed ahead of earnings.

text.p: Trading in individual equity options was mixed, with investors largely sidelined ahead of the onslaught of second quarter earnings, traders said Thursday.
"We were kind of busy at the beginning but things just died," one trader at a U.S. brokerage firm said. "I guess people are waiting for earnings."
He said most orders were blocks of less than 100 options.
The head of another brokerage's options department said his options trading desk was relatively quiet also.
Technology stock options were the feature, led by such names as 3Com Corp, Intel Corp and Gateway 2000 Inc.
On the Pacific Exchange, the 3Com July 50 and 55 calls and August 55 calls were fairly active as the stock rose 13/16 to 53-7/16 in heavy trading.
The stock rose sharply on Wednesday.
Also on the PCX, options on Compaq Computer Corp shares remained busy, led by the July 120 calls, which traded more than 3,400 contracts.

Compaq shares fell 1-1/4 to 119-3/4 after the computer maker reported second quarter earnings of $1.48 a share, better than analysts' consensus forecast of $1.39 but below some so-called "whisper" numbers, or unpublished estimates circulating on Wall Street.
At the American Stock Exchange (AMEX), perennial favorite Intel was active, particularly in the out-of-the-money July calls.
Intel shares fell 2-7/8 to 149-3/4 after a Salomon Brothers analyst said she was concerned the company's second quarter earnings may fall short of expectations.
The Intel July 150 call traded 5,645 contracts, the July 155 call traded nearly 4,000 and the July 160 call traded about 2,600.
Among Intel puts, the July 150 was most active with turnover of more than 3,400 contracts. The July 145 put traded 2,800.
Elsewhere, a couple of Gateway 2000 options were active at the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) in what a market maker said was a reverse conversion.
The Gateway August 40 put traded 7,030 contracts and the August 40 call traded 6,685.
The market maker explained the trading crowd was short underlying shares.

A reverse conversion, also known as a reversal, is a short underlying position combined with a synthetic long position. A synthetic long position is formed by selling puts and buying calls at the same strike price.
